title: Implement upgrade backoff and traffic dampening to prevent control-plane overload during Private/VPC upgrades
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: During the March 8th private deployment upgrade, multiple customer VPC clusters experienced transient control-plane unavailability when agent nodes restarted concurrently. Symptoms included API server 502/504 errors, large spike in control-plane CPU load, and a flood of reconnects that exhausted ephemeral ports on the orchestrator leading to cascading retries and a ~12 minute degradation window for affected clusters.

Root cause hypothesis: The rolling upgrade orchestration currently restarts agent workloads in parallel batches without a conservative reconnect/backoff strategy. When agents rejoined, they triggered large KV-store churn and a high rate of control-plane RPCs (healthchecks, session joins). The control-plane lacked a traffic-dampening mechanism for rejoin storms and did not apply progressive backoff on agent side.

Goals: 1) Prevent similar storms during future upgrades by introducing server-side dampening + client-side backoff. 2) Make upgrade sequencing safer (wave-based, dependent on health signals). 3) Add deterministic automated rollback and clearer runbook triggers.

Proposed solution (high level):
- Client (agent) changes: implement exponential jittered reconnect with configurable max parallel reconnections per node group. Add randomized startup delay window when a node restarts as part of an upgrade.
- Server/orchestrator changes: implement short-term token-bucket rate limiter for join/session RPCs and a soft-queue that prioritizes API calls over background reconciles during maintenance windows. Add circuit-breaker that temporarily rejects non-critical rejoin attempts when control-plane CPU or RPC latencies exceed thresholds.
- Orchestration changes: introduce upgrade waves with dynamic sizing (start with 5% of nodes), health gates based on API latency, KV-store commit rate, and ephemeral port utilization. If any gate trips, automatically pause and execute automatic rollback to previous version for the in-flight wave.
- Visibility & alarms: surface new metrics (reconnect-rate, join-queue-length, token-bucket-drop-rate) in Console, and add automated PagerDuty alerts when reconnect-rate or API error rate exceed thresholds during upgrades.

Acceptance criteria:
- New client backoff implemented and enabled behind feature flag.
- Orchestrator rate limiting and wave-based sequencing in prod config with default conservative values.
- Automated rollback triggers tested in staging and documented.
- Upgrade runbook updated with explicit checklists and required metrics to proceed to next wave.
- No outage-class customer impact observed in staged upgrade simulations (load tests and chaos experiments).

Testing plan:
- Unit + integration tests for agent reconnect jitter/backoff.
- Staging rollout: run orchestrated upgrade on a representative staging fleet with synthetic reconnect flaps and assert control-plane stays within latency SLOs.
- Chaos test: intentionally crash 20% of nodes simultaneously in a canary VPC and validate rate limiter and wave gating preserve API health.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge agent and orchestrator changes behind feature flags.
2) Canary enable on internal infra clusters for 48h.
3) Gradual enable on low-traffic customer clusters with monitoring and on-call presence.
4) Post-mortem review and parameter tuning, then wider rollout.

Owners & timeline:
- Engineering owner (orchestrator rate limiting + waves): Ethan Chen (2 sprints).
- Agent owner (client backoff + jitter): Priya Rao (1 sprint).
- Observability + runbooks: SRE (Samir Gupta) and Product (Lena Ortiz) (1 sprint).

Risks & open questions:
- Backoff reduces reconnection storm but may increase time-to-recover for individual agents; need to balance customer SLAs for short-lived restarts.
- Token-bucket rejects might surface as new client errors if client-side retries are aggressive; ensure coordination between client and server behaviors.
- Automated rollback complexity: ensure no split-brain if partial waves are rolled back.

Follow-ups (post-deploy):
- Collect 2 weeks of metrics and run a retrospective to tune defaults.
- Add a simulation harness to validate future upgrade parameters before customer rollout.
